A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Linear Patch research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, appendices, and checklists are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA, perplexity, and MMLU evaluations, together with component, distillation, calibration-size, and pruning-metric analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results comparing different calibration datasets in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same channel scaling in Hadamard space, fused patch matrix, and optional offline top-K logits distillation. The pruning integrations and optimization objective are retained; rewritten explanations and the new mathematical appendix do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: The evaluation corpora and tasks remain WikiText-2, C4, PTB, MMLU, and nine commonsense QA tasks. v2 Appendix D additionally uses PTB and C4 as Linear Patch calibration sources, expanding the calibration-domain scenarios beyond WikiText-2 without introducing a new benchmark family.

E2.justification: The retained LLaMA-2-7B and LLaMA-3-8B training-free PPL comparisons omit LLM-Pruner in v2 Table 2, while v2 Table 17 removes SLEB from the retained MMLU settings. Taylor+ and patched SLEB in the main PPL table were already evaluated in v1 Appendix F; they are not new comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled calibration-source comparison for LLaMA-2-7B with nine layers pruned. Existing settings remain unchanged, including five-shot MMLU, 128 calibration sequences of length 2048, and one-epoch AdamW fine-tuning on 5,000 sequences at learning rate 1e-4.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests sensitivity to calibration corpus, including matched versus mismatched calibration and evaluation sources. Earlier analyses of patch components, distillation targets, calibration size, distillation-data size, top-K selection, and pruning metrics are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark performance. The activation-scaling standard deviations and statistical-significance checklist response are unchanged.

E6.justification: The reported result coverage contracts substantially: much of v1 Table 15's PPL grid disappears, including Baichuan and DeepSeek PPL results, and v2 Table 17 omits the higher-pruning MMLU settings from v1 Table 16. Retained performance entries match, including the headline QA results. New Table 10 reports average PPL of 30.29, 30.40, and 30.52 for WikiText-2, PTB, and C4 calibration, respectively.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix G adds a mu-incoherence definition and an elementwise maximum bound in Equation 11, absent from v1. This is a limited formal addition: although presented as a Hadamard outlier-reduction proof, it does not establish that the proposed transformation satisfies the assumed incoherence condition.

C1.justification: Both versions attribute pruning degradation to activation-magnitude mismatch and propose the same fused patch with optional offline distillation. The main performance and efficiency claims, including 94.15% and 95.16% retained performance, remain unchanged despite extensive rewriting.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix D newly interprets calibration results as evidence of domain-specific benefits, stability under domain mismatch, and robustness to calibration-data quality. The existing limitation concerning uneven degradation across tasks is retained in a separate section.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link and states that code is available, whereas v1 only promises release upon acceptance. Appendix B newly specifies lm_eval version 0.4.4, and Appendix C identifies the model and pruning level for the existing calibration-size ablation. These are documentation additions, not evidence of changed implementation settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including BinaryBERT, QuIP, Prune&Comp, and additional quantization and model-merging work. It also expands discussion of the previously cited UIDL approach. The central positioning around correcting magnitude mismatch in layer pruning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. v2 separates limitations from the conclusion, adds broader-impact and acknowledgment sections, and moves the checklist ahead of the technical appendices.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the benchmark displays: a compact paired PPL table replaces much of the comprehensive appendix table, the MMLU table is condensed and restructured, and a calibration-data table is added. Some comparison tables lose pruning-ratio columns. Figures 1, 2, and 4 retain their plotted content; Figure 3 receives label and caption corrections.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, the calibration-source ablation, and additional reproducibility information provide benefits. However, removing substantial PPL and MMLU comparisons reduces empirical transparency, while passages still cite settings and comparisons absent from the revised tables. The newly claimed Hadamard proof also leaves its essential assumption unestablished. These weaknesses outweigh the limited additions, although the central method and primary QA evidence remain intact.
